LESSON: BUILDINGS IN THE NEIGHBOURHOOD

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Our Neighbourhood
Topic 4.2: Buildings in the neighbourhood
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Buildings in the neighbourhood, part of Our Neighbourhood in SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we have buildings in the neighbourhood? 2. How are buildings used in the environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Buildings in the neighbourhood together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Citizenship: learner develops sense of belonging when identifying the buildings in the neighbourhood and their uses.

Values:
Patriotism: learner enhances citizenship as they appreciate buildings in the neighbourhood.

Unity: learner enhances cooperation as they construct simple structures of buildings found in the neighbourhood.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Financial literacy: learner matches and pairs items sold in the market.

Link to other learning area:

Buildings found in the neighbourhood relates to places of worship in Religious Activities.

37

Suggested Learning Resources

Charts, picture cards, flash cards, braille cards, glue, crayons, coloured pencil, photos, sticks, paints, maize cobs, grass, video clips.
